_meta.rule: offer_inbox_receiver.py refuses unless a row here names the exact authorization id AND its status is `approved` AND its fixture_id, delivery_id, packet_path and packet_sha256 all match the packet reference exactly. A `draft` row admits nothing. A `spent` row admits nothing. Entries are never deleted: a spent one stays so its acknowledgement remains explained.
_meta.one_attempt: A row authorises ONE delivery. The receiver marks it `spent` once an acknowledgement exists. There are no retries: a refused or failed attempt stays failed and a further attempt needs a NEW owner decision and a NEW row.
_meta.enforcement: PREVENTIVE for this mechanism, unlike the skill registries. The receiver reads this file itself and checks every condition BEFORE creating a directory, opening an acknowledgement, changing registry state, running receiver logic or recording a delivered outcome. It deliberately does NOT consult the runtime approval flag, which is reported but never enforced.
_meta.scope: The Sector (01) -> Offer (02) packet-reference route only, to the offline fake Offer-side receiver. No event is published, no event bus is used, the runtime is never booted, and no external destination is reachable.

_field_notes.status: draft | approved | spent. Only `approved` admits a delivery.
_field_notes.sandbox_root: The receiver independently re-validates this: absolute, resolves to itself, no symlink or junction on its chain, not inside a git working tree, no `onedrive` component, and not a production or runtime-log location. A failure here refuses before any side effect.
_field_notes.packet_root: OPTIONAL, and additive. ABSENT: behaviour is exactly as before - packet_path must resolve inside sandbox_root, which bounds both the read and the write. PRESENT: packet_path must resolve inside packet_root instead, while the acknowledgement stays confined to sandbox_root. Both roots then pass EVERY safe-root check independently - absolute, resolving to themselves, no traversal, no symlink or junction on either chain, neither inside a git working tree, neither under OneDrive, and neither naming a repository, runtime-memory or fixture-log location.
_field_notes.same_fixture_requirement: When packet_root is present the receiver additionally requires: packet_root is named exactly `04_fixture_inputs`; sandbox_root is named exactly `05_outputs`; both resolve to the SAME parent directory, which is the authorised fixture root; that fixture root's directory NAME equals the authorisation's fixture_id (the mechanism's normalization rule - a fixture root is named for its fixture); packet_path is a DIRECT file inside packet_root, not nested; and the acknowledgement is a direct file inside sandbox_root. This is what refuses a cross-fixture read or write even when both paths are independently safe: roots under two different fixtures do not share a parent, and a parent whose name is not the fixture_id is not that authorisation's fixture.
_field_notes.packet_path: Re-validated to resolve INSIDE the authorised read root - sandbox_root when packet_root is absent, packet_root when it is present - with no `..` traversal and no link escape.
_field_notes.packet_sha256: Re-computed from the file at delivery time. A changed packet is refused with PACKET_HASH_MISMATCH.
